Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a message of felicitations to the Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Palestine, Mohammad Mustafa, on the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence of the State of Palestine.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives, I extend my sincere good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Palestine on the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence of the State of Palestine.

As you mark the 37th anniversary of Palestine’s Declaration of Independence, let me reaffirm the Maldives’ unwavering support for the Palestinian people in their rightful pursuit of independence and self-determination.

The Maldives remains firmly committed to supporting the Palestinian cause and strengthening the bonds of solidarity and brotherhood between our two nations. I look forward to continuing to work together with Your Excellency to advance the just cause of Palestine on the international stage.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: Maldives Co-Convenes the LDCs/SIDS Trust Fund Pledging Event
en.description: The Maldives, alongside the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), Finland, Mauritius, and Malawi, co-convened the LDCs/SIDS Trust Fund Pledging Event at the Palais des Nations, in Geneva, Switzerland…
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/361

The Maldives, alongside the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), Finland, Mauritius, and Malawi, co-convened the LDCs/SIDS Trust Fund Pledging Event at the Palais des Nations, in Geneva, Switzerland today. The pledging event successfully raised USD $238,500 to support the participation of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in effectively carrying out the work of the Human Rights Council.

The High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk graced his presence as the Chief Guest of the event. In his remarks, he underscored the importance of the Trust Fund in fostering inclusivity and amplifying the voices of SIDS and LDCs within the Council.

Speaking at the event, Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Office in Geneva, Ambassador Dr. Salma Rasheed, emphasised the critical importance of the Trust Fund for underrepresented nations such as the Maldives. She noted that as a co-lead in establishing the Trust Fund in 2012, and a direct beneficiary, the Maldives understands the value of the Trust Fund in empowering its diplomats to actively engage in global human rights discussions. Further, Ambassador Dr. Salma Rasheed, described the Fund as “a lifeline for SIDS and LDCs, providing the skills and resources needed to amplify” LDCs and SIDS’ voices in addressing “unique challenges on a global stage”.

The Trust Fund, which was established in 2012 and has been operational since 2014, ensures that SIDS and LDCS, particularly those states without permanent representation in Geneva can effectively engage with the Council. Moreover, it has been pivotal in enhancing inclusivity and diversity in global human rights discussions, enabling states to address pressing issues and advocate for the unique challenges faced by SIDS and LDCs. To date, the Fund has supported 281 officials from 71 countries and significantly strengthened their capacity to meaningfully contribute to the Human Rights Council’s work.

As a steadfast advocate of inclusivity, the Maldives wishes to express its gratitude to all donors for their continued generosity, which has been vital to the success and sustainability of the Trust Fund. The Maldives further expresses hope that the impact of the Trust Fund continues to expand and grow, with its beneficiaries gaining valuable experience and expertise that in turn, strengthens the long-term capacity of their countries to effectively contribute to the Human Rights Council’s functions and work.

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel sends congratulatory message to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a congratulatory message to Takeshi Iwaya, on his reappointment as the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan.
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/358

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a congratulatory message to Takeshi Iwaya, on his reappointment as the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“I am pleased to extend my heartfelt congratulations to Your Excellency on your reappointment as the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan. Your exemplary leadership and experience will undoubtedly bring great success during your tenure.

On 14 November, the Maldives and Japan will mark 57 years of the establishment of diplomatic relations, a friendship built on trust, shared values, and close collaboration across sectors, with people-to-people ties at the cornerstone of our enduring relations. Japan’s contributions have spanned across all corners of the Maldives, playing a significant role in fostering lasting economic prosperity, improving livelihoods, and enhancing the well-being of our people, with every Maldivian, both directly and indirectly, benefiting from Japan’s support towards our national development.

I am confident that under your leadership, our bilateral relations will continue to prosper and reach new heights. I look forward to working closely with Your Excellency to realize the full potential of our bilateral relationship and wish you every success in your new role.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr. Khaleel sends Independence Day greetings to Angola
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of External Relations of the Republic of Angola, Téte António on the occasion of Angola’s Independence Day.
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/357

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel has sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of External Relations of the Republic of Angola, Téte António on the occasion of Angola’s Independence Day.

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives, and on my own behalf, I extend warm greetings to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Angola on the joyous occasion of your Independence Day.

I look forward to working with Your Excellency to enhance the cooperation between our two countries.

Let me take this opportunity to extend my best wishes for your good health and well-being and for continued progress and prosperity for the people of Angola.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

dv.title: ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑރ. ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް، އެންގޯލާގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: އެންގޯލާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެ ޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޓޭޓޭ އެންޓޯނިއޯއަށް، ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑރ. ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/357

އެންގޯލާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެ ޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޓޭޓޭ އެންޓޯނިއޯއަށް، ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑރ. ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.

"ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި، އަދި އަޅުގަނޑުގެ އަމިއްލަ ނަމުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށާއި އެންގޯލާގެ ސަރުކާރަށް އަދި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާއާއި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް އަރިސްކުރަމެވެ.

އެންގޯލާއާއި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާ ދެމެދު އޮތް ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކުރުމަށް މަނިފާނާއެކު މަސައްކަތްކުރުމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު ތައްޔާރަށް ހުރިކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން އަރުވަމެވެ.

އަދި މި ފުރުޞަތުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށް ދުޅަހެޔޮ ޞިއްޙަތާއި އެންގޯލާގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިއެރުމާއި ފާގަތިކަންލިބުމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު އެދެމެވެ.

އަޅުގަނޑު މަނިކުފާނަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އާކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކޮށް އެރުވުމަށް މި ފުރުޞަތުގެ ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ.

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr Khaleel urges for renewed commitment to address the plight of the Palestinian people
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel participated in the preparatory meeting at the level of Foreign Ministers held today in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, ahead of the Extraordinary Joint Arab-Islamic Summit to…
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/356

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel participated in the preparatory meeting at the level of Foreign Ministers held today in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, ahead of the Extraordinary Joint Arab-Islamic Summit to be held on 11 November 2024.

In his remarks, Minister Dr. Khaleel expressed deep concern over the increased suffering of the Palestinian people, reflecting on the escalating violence and genocidal acts perpetrated by Israel. Emphasizing the collective responsibility of the Islamic Ummah in alleviating the suffering of the Palestinian people, Dr. Khaleel called for concerted action that go beyond statements of solidarity. He urged the international community to take decisive measures to hold Israel accountable for the continuous violations of international and humanitarian laws and urged countries to work across multiple platforms, including the UN Security Council and the International Court of Justice.  
  
Minister Dr Khaleel reaffirmed the commitment of Maldives to strengthen cooperation with the Islamic countries in the pursuit of justice and peace for Palestinian people. He also noted that establishment of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine, based on the pre-1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital, as fundamental to achieve a lasting and just resolution to the situation.  
  
The Joint Arab-Islamic Summit is being convened by the Government of the Kingdom of the Saudi Arabia in coordination with the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the League of Arab States, to address and explore actionable solutions to the ongoing sufferings of the Palestine and Lebanon.

ENDS

dv.title: ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންގެ ހައްޤުގައި އިތުރަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރުމަށް ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑޮކްޓަރ ޚަލީލް އިލްތިމާސްކުރައްވައިފި
dv.description: ސައުދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާގެ ރިޔާދުގައި މި ނޮވެމްބަރު މަހުގެ 11 ގައި ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ "އެކްސްޓްރާއޯޑިނަރީ ޖޮއިންޓް އަރަބް-އިސްލާމިކް ސަމިޓް" އަށް ތައްޔާރުވުމުގެ ގޮތުން ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ފެންވަރުގައި މިއަދު ބޭއްވި…
dv.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/356

ސައުދީ ޢަރަބިއްޔާގެ ރިޔާދުގައި މި ނޮވެމްބަރު މަހުގެ 11 ގައި ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ "އެކްސްޓްރާއޯޑިނަރީ ޖޮއިންޓް އަރަބް-އިސްލާމިކް ސަމިޓް" އަށް ތައްޔާރުވުމުގެ ގޮތުން ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ފެންވަރުގައި މިއަދު ބޭއްވި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި އެމަނިކުފާނު ދެއްވި ތަޤްރީރުގައި، އިސްރާއީލުން މެދުކެނޑުމެއްނެތި ފަލަސްތީނަށް ދެމުންގެންދާ ހަމަލާތަކާއި ހިންގަމުންދާ ނަސްލުނައްތާލުމުގެ އަމަލުތައް ހަރުކަށި އިބާރާތުން ކުށްވެރިކޮށް، ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ކުރިމަތިވާ އަނިޔާތަކަށް ލުޔެއް ލިބިފައިނުވާތީ އެކަމާމެދު ކަންބޮޑުވުން ފާޅުކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުން ތަހައްމަލްކުރަމުންދާ އަނިޔާތަކުން އަރައިގަތުމަށް އެހީވުމަކީ މުޅި އިސްލާމީ އުންމަތުގެ ޒިންމާއެއްކަމުގައި ފާހަގަކުރައްވައި، މި މަގުގައި އަމަލީ މަސައްކަތްކުރުމަށް ގޮވާލެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި އިސްރާއީލުން ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ޤާނޫނާ ޚިލާފަށް ހިންގަމުންގެންދާ އަމަލުތައް ކުއްވެރިކޮށް ވަކި ގައުމެއް އިސްތިސްނާ ނުވާނެހެން ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ޤާނޫނު ތަންފީޒުކުރުމަށްވެސް ގޮވާލެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި އ.ދ. ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލިސް އަދި އިންޓަނޭޝަނަލް ކޯޓް އޮފް ޖަސްޓިސް (އައި.ސީ.ޖޭ.) ފަދަ ޕްލެޓްފޯމްތަކުގައި އިސްރާއީލް ޖަވާބްދާރީކުރުމަށް ކުރަންޖެހޭ މަސައްކަތްތައް ކުރުމަށްވެސް އެމަނިކުފާނު ގޮވާލައްވާފައެވެ.

މީގެ އިތުރުން، ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ހައްގުގައި ވަކާލާތުކުރުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އަބަދުވެސް ދެމިއޮންނާނެކަމުގެ ޔަގީންކަން ދެއްވައި، އިސްލާމީ ގައުމުތަކާއެކު ފަލަސްތީނުގެ މައްސަލައަށް ހައްލެއް ހޯދުމަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރުމަށް ފަސްނުޖެހެނޭ ކަމަށް ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ. ހަމައެއާއެކު، މި ހަނގުރާމައަށް އޮތް ހަމައެކަނި ދެމެހެއްޓެނިވި ހައްލަކީ 1967 ގެ ކުރިން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ބޯޑަރުތަކާ އެއްގޮތްވާ ގޮތުގެމަތިން، އިރުމަތީ ޤުދުސް އަކީ އެ ގައުމުގެ ވެރިކަންކުރާ ރަށް ކަމަށް ކަނޑައަޅައި، ފަލަސްތީން އިސްރާއީލުގެ އަތްދަށުން މިނިވަންކޮށް، އެއީ މިނިވަން، މުސްތަޤިއްލު އަދި އަމިއްލަ ސިޔާދަތީ ބާރު ހިނގާ ގައުމަކަށް ހެދުންކަމުގައި އެ މަނިކުފާނު ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ.

ނޮވެމްބަރ މަހުގެ 11 ވަނަ ދުވަހުގައި ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ އެކްސްޓްރާއޯޑިނަރީ ޖޮއިންޓް އަރަބް-އިސްލާމިކް ސަމިޓަކީ ސައުދީއަރަބިއްޔާގެ ސަރުކާރާއި އޯގަނައިޒޭޝަން އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް ކޯޕަރޭޝަން (އޯ.އައި.ސީ.) އާއި ލީގް އޮފް އަރަބް ސްޓޭޓްސް އާ ގުޅިގެން ފަލަސްތީން އަދި ލުބްނާނަށް އިސްރާއީލުން ދެމުން ގެންދާ ހަމަލާތަކަށް ހައްލެއް ހޯދުމަށް މަޝްވަރާކުރުމަށްޓަކައި ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ބައްދަލުވުމެކެވެ.

en.title: The first round of political-bilateral consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania was held today
en.description: The first round of political-bilateral consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania was held today.
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/355

The first round of political-bilateral consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania was held today.

The political-bilateral consultations serve as a vital platform for both countries to engage on important issues of mutual interest, spanning bilateral, regional, and multilateral concerns.

During the consultations, both sides explore avenues to deepen bilateral ties and enhance cooperation across key sectors, including education, culture, environment and climate change.

Special emphasis was placed on strengthening collaboration in the tourism industry, with focus on improving connectivity and fostering people-to-people exchanges.

The consultations also provided an opportunity to address pressing international and regional issues, with both sides reaffirming commitment to closer cooperation in multilateral forums, in line with shared values and priorities.

The first round of political-bilateral consultations was co-chaired by Ambassador Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary Bilateral at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and Ambassador Traian Laurențiu Hristea - Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania.

ENDS

en.title: Emperor of Japan confers Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star upon former Maldives Ambassador to Japan, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel
en.description: On 06 November 2024, His Majesty the Emperor of Japan conferred the “Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star” upon H.E. Mr. Ahmed Khaleel, former Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to Japan and former Minister…
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/354

On 06 November 2024, His Majesty the Emperor of Japan conferred the “Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star” upon H.E. Mr. Ahmed Khaleel, former Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to Japan and former Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, in recognition of his invaluable contributions to strengthening the friendship between Japan and the Maldives. This marks the first time a Maldivian national has received this prestigious honour.

A dedicated diplomat, with over 41 years of experience in the Maldives Foreign Service, Ambassador Khaleel is among the very few who have consistently risen through the ranks to the highest echelons of diplomacy since he joined foreign service. During his tenure as Ambassador to Japan, he worked tirelessly to elevate Maldives-Japan bilateral relations. Following the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami in 2011, he organised a symbolic donation of over 700,000 fish cans to Japan, contributing to strong ties between the peoples of both countries. Furthermore, Amb. Khaleel’s efforts led to transformative development projects funded by Japanese grants, benefiting key sectors across the Maldives. His commitment to fostering ties at various levels has been instrumental in cementing the friendly bonds and goodwill shared between Japan and the Maldives, especially in building meaningful people-to-people contact between the two countries. Amb. Khaleel retired from the Maldives Foreign Service in 2023.

The decoration of the Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star is one of the orders under the Order of the Rising Sun, established in 1875 by Emperor Meiji, awarded by the Emperor of Japan to both Japanese and foreign individuals in recognition of meritorious service over a long duration.

en.title: Maldives to Participate in the 47th Session of the UPR Working Group
en.description: The 47th Session of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) commenced at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, today. The session will continue for a period of two weeks and will conclude on 15 November 2024. During this…
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/353

The 47th Session of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) commenced at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, today. The session will continue for a period of two weeks and will conclude on 15 November 2024. During this Session, fourteen States will undergo the review of their respective human rights records. The countries to be reviewed are Albania, Bhutan, Brunei Darussalam, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Costa Rica, Cote d’Ivoire, Dominica, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, Nicaragua, Norway, Portugal and Qatar.

The UPR Working Group holds three sessions annually. The Fourth Cycle review of the UPR began in November 2022 and will conclude in 2027. The UPR is a State-driven process which involves a review of the overall situation of human rights of all UN Member States. This UN mechanism provides the States under review with the opportunity to declare the progress made in fulfilling their human rights obligations and commitments in their respective countries. It also allows fellow Member States to provide constructive recommendations on how the States under review can further improve the implementation of their human rights obligations. Each State review is further facilitated by groups of three States, known as “troikas”, who serve as rapporteurs. The Maldives as a member of the Human Rights Council has been selected to be represented in the Troika for the review of Qatar.

The Maldives delegation for the 47th Session of the UPR will be led by Dr. Salma Rasheed, Ambassador and Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Office at Geneva, and will be accompanied by Counsellor Mr. Adam Hamid, Counsellor Uza. Aminath Shifaya Ibrahim, Second Secretary Ms. Maryam Fathika Fayaz, and Attaché Mr. Raaidh Saeedh, from the Permanent Mission. In line with the Government’s key policies and priorities, the Maldives delegation will actively engage and provide constructive recommendations during this UPR Session.

ENDS

dv.title: ޔުނިވަރސަލް ޕީރިއަޑިކް ރިވިއުގެ 47 ވަނަ ސެޝަންގައި ރާއްޖެއިން ބައިވެރިވަނީ
dv.description: ޔުނިވަރސަލް ޕީރިއޮޑިކް ރިވިއު (ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު.) ގެ 47 ވަނަ ބައްދަލުވުން ސްވިޒަލޭންޑްގެ ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަ އ.ދ ގެ އޮފީހުގައި މިއަދު ފަށައިފިއެވެ. ދެ ހަފްތާގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް ކުރިއަށްދާ މި ސެޝަން، މި ހިނގާ ނޮވެމްބަރ މަހުގެ 4 އިން…
dv.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/353

ޔުނިވަރސަލް ޕީރިއޮޑިކް ރިވިއު (ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު.) ގެ 47 ވަނަ ބައްދަލުވުން ސްވިޒަލޭންޑްގެ ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަ އ.ދ ގެ އޮފީހުގައި މިއަދު ފަށައިފިއެވެ. ދެ ހަފްތާގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް ކުރިއަށްދާ މި ސެޝަން، މި ހިނގާ ނޮވެމްބަރ މަހުގެ 4 އިން 15 ގެ ނިޔަލަށް ހިނގަމުންދާނެއެވެ. މި ސެޝަންގައި 14 ޤައުމެއްގައި އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތައް ނަގަހައްޓާ މިންވަރު ވަޒަންކުރުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. މި 14 ޤައުމަކީ އަލްބޭނިއާ، ބޫޓާން، ބްރުނާއި ދާރުއްސަލާމް، ޑިމޮކްރެޓިކް ރިޕަބްލިކް އޮފް ދަ ކޮންގޯ، ކޮސްޓަ ރީކާ، ކޮޓް ޑިވުއާ، ޑޮމިނިކާ، އިކުއިޓޯރިއަލް ގިނީ، އިތިއޯޕިއާ، ޑިމޮކްރެޓިކް ޕީޕަލްސް ރިޕަބްލިކް އޮފް ކޮރެއާ، ނިކަރާގުއާ، ނޯރވޭ، ޕޯޗުގަލް އަދި ޤަތަރެވެ.

ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު. ވަރކިންގ ގްރޫޕުގެ 3 ބައްދަލުވުމެއް އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ ކައުންސިލުގައި ކޮންމެ އަހަރަކު ބާއްވައެވެ. އެގޮތުން، 2022 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ ނޮވެމްބަރު މަހުން ފެށިގެން މިހާރު ކުރިއަށްދާ 4 ވަނަ ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު. ސައިކަލް 2027 ވަނަ އަހަރާ ހަމައަށް ކުރިއަށްދާނެއެވެ. ޔުނިވަރސަލް ޕީރިއަޑިކް ރިވިއުއަކީ އ.ދ. ގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމުތަކުގައި އިންސާނީ ހައްޤުތަކުގެ ޙާލަތު ވަޒަންކޮށް ދެނެގަތުމަށް އެ ޖަމުޢިއްޔާއިން ކަނޑައަޅާފައިވާ ނިޒާމެކެވެ. އަދި އިންސާނީ ހައްޤުތަކުގެ ޙާލަތު ރަނގަޅުކުރުމަށާއި، އިންސާނީ ހައްޤުތައް ކަށަވަރުކުރުމުގައި މެމްބަރު ޤައުމުތަކުން ހޯދާފައިވާ ކުރިއެރުން އ.ދ ގެ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ ކައުންސިލަށް ހުށަހެޅުމުގެ ފުރުޞަތު، ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު. މެދުވެރިކޮށް އެ ޤައުމުތަކަށް ލިބެއެވެ. ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު. ގެ ނިޒާމު ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވަނީ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ އިލްތިޒާމުތައް އުފުލުމުގައި މެންބަރު ޤައުމުތަކުން އިތުރަށް ރަނގަޅުކުރަން ފެންނަ ކަންކަން ހުށަހަޅައި، އެޤައުމުތަކުން ކުރަމުން އަންނަ މަސައްކަތް އަގުވަޒަންކުރެވޭނެ ފަދަ ގޮތަކަށެވެ.

ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު. ވަރކިން ގްރޫޕްގެ ބައްދަލުވުންތަކުގައި ކަނޑައެޅިފައިވާ ކޮންމެ ޤައުމެއްގެ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކުގެ ޙާލަތު ވަޒަންކުރުމަށް އެހީތެރިވުމުގެ ގޮތުން އ.ދ. ގެ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ ކައުންސިލްގެ ތިން މެމްބަރުން "ޓްރޮއިކާ" ގެ ގޮތުގައި ހަރަކާތްތެރިވެއެވެ. އެގޮތުން، މިފަހަރުގެ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި އ.ދ. ގެ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާ ބެހޭ ކައުންސިލްގެ މެމްބަރެއްގެ ހައިސިއްޔަތުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ޤަތަރުގެ ރިވިއުގައި ޓްރޮއިކާ ގެ މެމްބަރުކަން ކުރާނެއެވެ.

ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު. ގެ 47 ވަނަ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ބައިވެރިވާ ވަފުދުގައި އެންމެ އިސްކޮށް ހުންނަވާނީ ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަ އދ.ގެ އޮފީހާއި އެހެނިހެން ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ޖަމުޢިއްޔާތަކަށް ކަނޑައަޅާފައި ހުންނަ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބު ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ރަޝީދެވެ. އަދި މިވަފުދުގައި ކައުންސެލަރ އަލްފާޟިލް އާދަމް ހާމިދު، ކައުންސެލަރ އަލްއުސްތާޛާ އާމިނަތު ޝިފާޔާ އިބްރާހީމް، ސެކަންޑް ސެކްރެޓަރީ އަލްފާޟިލާ މަރްޔަމް ފާތިކާ ފަޔާޒް އަދި އެޓާޝޭ އަލްފާޟިލް މުޙައްމަދު ރާއިދު ސައީދު ހިމެނެއެވެ. މިފަހަރުގެ ޔޫ.ޕީ.އާރު. ބައްދަލުވުމުގައިވެސް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ވަފުދުން ބައިވެރިވެ، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ މުހިންމު ސިޔާސަތުތަކާ އެއްގޮތްވާ ގޮތުގެ މަތިން ބިނާކުރަނިވި އިސްލާޙުތަކެއް ރިވިއު ކުރެވޭ ޤައުމުތަކަށް ހުށަހަޅާނެއެވެ.

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Panama
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Panama, Javier Martínez Acha Vásquez on the occasion of the…
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/352

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Panama, Javier Martínez Acha Vásquez on the occasion of the Independence Day of Panama.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, I would like to extend warm greetings and best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Panama, on the occasion of your Independence Day.

I believe that our joint efforts on common issues will foster an even stronger relationship in the years ahead.

Let me extend my best wishes for your good health and well-being and for the peace and prosperity of the people of Panama.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

dv.title: ‏ ޕެނަމާގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް އެ ގައުމުގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: ‏‎ ޕެނަމާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ހާވިއެރ މާރޓިނެޒް އަޗާ ވަޒްކަސް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/352

‏‎ ޕެނަމާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ހާވިއެރ މާރޓިނެޒް އަޗާ ވަޒްކަސް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.

މިނިސްޓަރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި މިވަނީއެވެ.

"ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި، އަދި އަޅުގަނޑުގެ އަމިއްލަ ނަމުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށާއި ޕެނަމާ ސަރުކާރަށާއި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް، ޕެނަމާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް އަރިސްކުރަމެވެ.

ރާއްޖެއާއި ޕެނަމާއާ ދެމެދު އޮތް އެކުވެރިކަމުގެ ގުޅުން ކުރިއަށް އޮތް އަހަރުތަކުގައިވެސް އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިވެގެންދާނެކަން އަޅުގަނޑަށް ޔަގީނެވެ.

މަނިކުފާނަށް ދުޅަހެޔޮ ސިއްޙަތާއި ޕެނެމާގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ސުލްހައާއި ތަނަވަސްކަން ލިބުމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު އެދެމެވެ.

‏‎އަޅުގަނޑު މަނިކުފާނަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އާކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކޮށް އެރުވުމަށް މި ފުރުސަތުގެ ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ."

ނިމުނީ

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of The Federated States of Micronesia
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Secretary for Foreign Affairs of the Federated States of Micronesia, Hon. Lorin S. Robert on the…
en.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/351

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Dr. Abdulla Khaleel sends message of felicitations to the Secretary for Foreign Affairs of the Federated States of Micronesia, Hon. Lorin S. Robert on the occasion of the Independence Day of The Federated States of Micronesia.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, I would like to extend warm greetings to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of The Federated States of Micronesia, on the occasion of your Independence Day.

As fellow small island developing states, I am confident that the collaboration between our countries will deepen in the coming years as we work together on areas of common interests.

Let me extend my best wishes for your good health and well-being and for the peace and prosperity of the people of The Federated States of Micronesia.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

dv.title: ‏މައިކްރޮނީޝިއާގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް އެ ގައުމުގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: ‏‎ މައިކްރޮނީޝިއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ލޯރިން ރޮބަރޓް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
Ref: 2024/PR/351

‏‎ މައިކްރޮނީޝިއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ލޯރިން ރޮބަރޓް އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަބްދުﷲ ޚަލީލް ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފިއެވެ.

މިނިސްޓަރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި މިވަނީއެވެ.

"ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި، އަދި އަޅުގަނޑުގެ އަމިއްލަ ނަމުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށާއި މައިކްރޮނީޝިއާ ސަރުކާރަށާއި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް، މައިކްރޮނީޝިއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި އިހްލާސްތެރި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް އަރިސްކުރަމެވެ.

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި މައިކްރޯނޭޝިއާ އަކީ ކުދި ޖަޒީރާ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ހިމެނޭ ދެ ޤައުމު ކަމުގައިވާތީ، ރާއްޖެއާއި މައިކްރޮނީޝިއާ އާ ދެމެދު އޮތް އެކުވެރިކަމުގެ ގުޅުން ކުރިއަށް އޮތް އަހަރުތަކުގައިވެސް އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިވެގެންދާނެކަން އަޅުގަނޑަށް ޔަގީނެވެ.

މަނިކުފާނަށް ދުޅަހެޔޮ ސިއްޙަތާއި މައިކްރޮނީޝިއާގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ސުލްހައާއި ތަނަވަސްކަން ލިބުމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު އެދެމެވެ.

‏‎އަޅުގަނޑު މަނިކުފާނަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އާކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކޮށް އެރުވުމަށް މި ފުރުސަތުގެ ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ."

ނިމުނީ
